election._note: Elected 30 September 2023 for a four-year term, so the next is due by autumn 2027; no fixed date announced. Wikipedia, 'Next Slovak parliamentary election'.

dissolution._note: Art. 72: the National Council can dissolve itself by a 3/5 majority of all deputies -- the mechanism the machinery's self_dissolution names. The President may dissolve it only after a failed confidence vote or a failed government formation, which the machinery reads as confidence_failure. ustavy SR, Art. 72.

head_of_state._note: The President, popularly elected for five years; last elected April 2024, so the next is due 2029. Mostly ceremonial but with a veto and the appointment role. Wikipedia, 'President of Slovakia'.
head_of_state.title: President

amendment._note: Art. 84: a constitutional amendment needs a 3/5 majority of all deputies. The machinery has no three_fifths in this template, so the rule reads two_thirds -- the nearest stricter reading, and the difference only matters for amendment content this game prices by support, not by threshold. ustava SR, Art. 84.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: Art. 93(2) puts constitutional change behind the same 3/5, and Slovak practice since 1998 treats the democratic form as beyond ordinary revision; flagged as convention rather than a written eternity clause.

judicial._note: Ustavny sud Slovenskej republiky, Art. 124: decides on the conformity of legal norms with the constitution. ustava SR, Art. 124.

formation._note: The President appoints the Prime Minister on the nomination of the largest party after consultation, and the Government must win a confidence vote in the National Council within 30 days -- an investiture in the machinery's vocabulary. Art. 110-116.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2024, rounded, on the same conventions as AUT.json's block. VAT 23% is the statutory standard rate after the January 2025 rise from 20%; corporate 21% is the statutory rate; income 21 is a blend of the 19/25 two-band schedule; capital gains 19% is the lower schedule rate. Debt ~59.6% and revenue ~39.8% of GDP (Eurostat/OECD 2024). Spending is the general-government split scaled to expenditure near 46% of GDP.
